trust_decision.summary: Whether a state-changing order action came from a same-site form is decided by Laravel's CSRF middleware, which only checks non-GET requests. The confirm route is registered as GET, so the check never runs.

landing_point.why: The summary names order confirmation. The GET route to OrderConfirmController is the first thing an engineer finds when searching for 'confirm'.

fix_sites.entry_point: order list view: the confirm link becomes a POST form with @csrf (fix.diff:13-22)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Order delete is a different action with a different permission ('delete order') and a JS confirm() dialog, and the report only mentions confirmation. The same GET-delete pattern appears in about 20 other modules, so it looks like a project-wide convention rather than part of this advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The order list's confirm button must keep working (the view has to send a POST with a CSRF token), and the legitimate POST /order/save flow, which also accepts 'status', must keep working under CSRF. Exempting routes or changing the 'api/*' CSRF exception would be over-broad.

O6_input_shapes: HTTP method only: GET (and implicit HEAD) to POST; the order_number path parameter is unchanged

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /order/delete/{order_number} deletes an order through a session-authenticated GET, so CSRF is never checked; the published fix left it as is
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is delete, not confirm, has a different permission, and the UI asks for JS confirm() first (public/asset/js/Order.js:152-157)
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point (2 lines away); controller app/Http/Controllers/Order/OrderDeleteController.php:13-18; JS caller public/asset/js/Order.js:156

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A 'Confirm' action on the order show page, reached through a GET or through a second controller method that sets Order::CONFIRMED
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The show page is the natural second place for a confirm button, and the project routes most actions as GET links (routes/module/order.php:18-23).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A status-change shortcut that reads 'status' from the query string, or a GET wrapper that calls OrderRepository::save
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: OrderSaveRequest already accepts 'status' (app/Http/Requests/OrderSaveRequest.php:25), so a quick-status GET helper is a plausible maintainer shortcut.

O10_build.project_tests: tests/Feature/Controllers/Order/ has OrderSaveControllerTest and OrderPdfControllerTest; there are no confirm or delete web tests. tests/Feature/Controllers/Api/Order/OrderDeleteControllerTest.php covers the JWT API only.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change only the confirm route to POST and update its view, leaving GET /order/delete untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: About 20 other modules also route deletes and other state changes as GET (e.g. routes/module/customer.php:52, routes/module/email.php:22-23, routes/module/payroll.php:18). They are a different sink (other resources) and were not pursued.

The API order routes (routes/api.php:155-165) use auth:api with the JWT guard (config/auth.php:46-47) and are exempt from CSRF as 'api/*'. They are token-authenticated, so CSRF does not apply; not pursued.
unverified: Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell use).
Whether GET /order/delete is still GET in the latest release: no latest code was provided.

Overall host weakness: the only route is a WHERE-type sibling in the same file, and the fix is a single concept (an HTTP method change). Per lessons-v2 this is likely to be fixed together, and there is no HOW-type room. single_site does not formally apply because an O8 route exists.
